text: The Standard Current Account is open to personal customers aged 18 or over. There is no monthly fee for the Standard Current Account. The fee, where there is one, is taken on the first working day of the month. Statements are issued monthly and are free online; a paper statement costs GBP 2 each.

Holders of the Standard Current Account can withdraw up to GBP 450 a day from cash machines. Payments made in online banking or the mobile app are limited to GBP 20,000 a day for the Standard Current Account. Limits reset at midnight UK time. A branch can raise a limit for a single day after an identity check.

An arranged overdraft on the Standard Current Account has an interest-free buffer of GBP 50. Borrowing above the buffer is charged daily. Unarranged borrowing is refused where possible and no fee is charged for a refused payment.

A replacement debit card for the Standard Current Account arrives within 5 working days. Card payments in a foreign currency on the Standard Current Account carry a fee of 2.75% of the amount. A lost card can be frozen in the app at once.

The Premier Current Account is open to customers who pay in at least GBP 5,000 a month. The monthly fee is GBP 18 for the Premier Current Account. The fee, where there is one, is taken on the first working day of the month. Statements are issued monthly and are free online; a paper statement costs GBP 2 each.

Holders of the Premier Current Account can withdraw up to GBP 900 a day from cash machines. Payments made in online banking or the mobile app are limited to GBP 75,000 a day for the Premier Current Account. Limits reset at midnight UK time. A branch can raise a limit for a single day after an identity check.

An arranged overdraft on the Premier Current Account has an interest-free buffer of GBP 500. Borrowing above the buffer is charged daily. Unarranged borrowing is refused where possible and no fee is charged for a refused payment.

A replacement debit card for the Premier Current Account arrives within 2 working days. Card payments in a foreign currency on the Premier Current Account carry a fee of 0% of the amount, that is, no fee. A lost card can be frozen in the app at once.

The Student Current Account is open to students on a course of two years or longer. There is no monthly fee for the Student Current Account. The fee, where there is one, is taken on the first working day of the month. Statements are issued monthly and are free online; a paper statement costs GBP 2 each.

Holders of the Student Current Account can withdraw up to GBP 300 a day from cash machines. Payments made in online banking or the mobile app are limited to GBP 5,000 a day for the Student Current Account. Limits reset at midnight UK time. A branch can raise a limit for a single day after an identity check.

An arranged overdraft on the Student Current Account has an interest-free buffer of GBP 1,500. Borrowing above the buffer is charged daily. Unarranged borrowing is refused where possible and no fee is charged for a refused payment.

A replacement debit card for the Student Current Account arrives within 5 working days. Card payments in a foreign currency on the Student Current Account carry a fee of 2.75% of the amount. A lost card can be frozen in the app at once.

The Business Start Account is open to businesses in their first two years of trading. The monthly fee is GBP 7.5 for the Business Start Account. The fee, where there is one, is taken on the first working day of the month. Statements are issued monthly and are free online; a paper statement costs GBP 2 each.

Holders of the Business Start Account can withdraw up to GBP 600 a day from cash machines. Payments made in online banking or the mobile app are limited to GBP 40,000 a day for the Business Start Account. Limits reset at midnight UK time. A branch can raise a limit for a single day after an identity check.

An arranged overdraft on the Business Start Account has an interest-free buffer of GBP 0. Borrowing above the buffer is charged daily. Unarranged borrowing is refused where possible and no fee is charged for a refused payment.

A replacement debit card for the Business Start Account arrives within 4 working days. Card payments in a foreign currency on the Business Start Account carry a fee of 2.95% of the amount. A lost card can be frozen in the app at once.

The Business Plus Account is open to businesses with turnover above GBP 2 million. The monthly fee is GBP 25 for the Business Plus Account. The fee, where there is one, is taken on the first working day of the month. Statements are issued monthly and are free online; a paper statement costs GBP 2 each.

Holders of the Business Plus Account can withdraw up to GBP 1,500 a day from cash machines. Payments made in online banking or the mobile app are limited to GBP 250,000 a day for the Business Plus Account. Limits reset at midnight UK time. A branch can raise a limit for a single day after an identity check.

An arranged overdraft on the Business Plus Account has an interest-free buffer of GBP 2,000. Borrowing above the buffer is charged daily. Unarranged borrowing is refused where possible and no fee is charged for a refused payment.

A replacement debit card for the Business Plus Account arrives within 2 working days. Card payments in a foreign currency on the Business Plus Account carry a fee of 1.5% of the amount. A lost card can be frozen in the app at once.
Holders of the Standard Current Account can withdraw up to GBP 300 a day from cash machines. Payments made in online banking are limited to GBP 10,000 a day. This version was replaced in March 2024.

section: Eligibility and fees (version of June 2022, superseded)
text: The monthly fee is GBP 5 for the Business Start Account, taken on the first working day of the month. This version was replaced in April 2024.

The purchase rate on the Classic Credit Card is 24.9% APR. Taking cash on the Classic Credit Card costs 3% of the amount, with a minimum of GBP 3. Interest on cash is charged from the day of the withdrawal.

The minimum payment on the Classic Credit Card is 2.5% of the balance or GBP 5, whichever is higher. A payment that arrives after the due date costs GBP 12. Customers can set a direct debit for the minimum, a fixed sum or the full balance.

The purchase rate on the Platinum Credit Card is 19.9% APR. Taking cash on the Platinum Credit Card costs 2.5% of the amount, with a minimum of GBP 3. Interest on cash is charged from the day of the withdrawal.

The minimum payment on the Platinum Credit Card is 2% of the balance or GBP 5, whichever is higher. A payment that arrives after the due date costs GBP 12. Customers can set a direct debit for the minimum, a fixed sum or the full balance.

The purchase rate on the Business Credit Card is 21.4% APR. Taking cash on the Business Credit Card costs 3.5% of the amount, with a minimum of GBP 3. Interest on cash is charged from the day of the withdrawal.

The minimum payment on the Business Credit Card is 5% of the balance or GBP 5, whichever is higher. A payment that arrives after the due date costs GBP 15. Customers can set a direct debit for the minimum, a fixed sum or the full balance.

Hotel rooms are booked through the travel desk. The nightly cap is GBP 210 in London, GBP 140 in other UK cities and GBP 190 overseas. A room above the cap needs written approval from a director before travel.
Staff who use their own car claim 45 pence a mile for the first 10,000 miles in a tax year and 25 pence a mile after that. Parking is claimed at cost. Fines are never reimbursed.
When travelling overnight, staff may claim up to GBP 35 for an evening meal and GBP 12 for breakfast if it is not included in the room rate. Alcohol is not reimbursed.

Claims are entered in the ExpenseHub system within 60 days of the spend. A receipt is required for any item above GBP 10. Claims older than 60 days are paid only with the approval of the finance director.
A line manager approves claims up to GBP 500. A claim above GBP 500 also needs a director. Approvers must not approve their own claims or those of their own manager.

Every complaint is acknowledged in writing within 3 working days. A final response is sent within 8 weeks of the day the complaint was received. If the deadline will be missed, the customer is told why and when to expect a reply.
A complaint handler can offer a goodwill payment of up to GBP 250. A team leader can approve up to GBP 1,000. Anything higher goes to the head of customer relations.
Complaints are logged in CaseTrack on the day they are received, including complaints resolved on the first call. The log records the product, the cause and the amount of any redress.
A complaint from a customer flagged as vulnerable is passed to the specialist support team within 1 working day. The team can pause collections activity for up to 30 days while the complaint is open.

Enhanced due diligence is required when cash paid into an account exceeds GBP 9,000 in any 30 days, when the customer is a politically exposed person, or when the customer is established in a high-risk country.

Customer records are reviewed every 12 months for high-risk customers, every 36 months for medium-risk customers and every 60 months for low-risk customers. A change of ownership triggers a review at once.
A member of staff who suspects money laundering sends an internal report to the nominated officer within 24 hours. The customer must not be told that a report has been made.
Form KYC-7 is completed for every person who owns or controls more than 25% of a business customer. Identity documents are kept for 5 years after the relationship ends.

Passwords are at least 14 characters long. Privileged accounts change their password every 90 days; other accounts change it only after a suspected compromise. Multi-factor authentication is required for all remote access.
A lost or stolen laptop or phone is reported to the Service Desk on extension 4400 within 1 hour. The device is wiped remotely as soon as it next connects.

Critical security patches are applied within 7 days of release and high-severity patches within 30 days. A system that cannot be patched needs a risk acceptance signed by the chief information security officer.
USB storage devices are blocked on all bank laptops. An exception lasts at most 14 days and is approved by the head of security operations.
A borrower can take a payment holiday of up to 3 months in any 12-month period, provided the account is not in arrears. Interest continues to accrue during the holiday.
Borrowers on a fixed rate can overpay up to 10% of the outstanding balance each year without a charge. Overpayments above that are subject to the early repayment charge.
The early repayment charge is 3% of the amount repaid in the first year of a fixed rate, 2% in the second year and 1% in the third year. No charge applies after the fixed rate ends.
The arrears team contacts the borrower after 1 missed payment. A field agent visit is arranged after 3 missed payments. Legal action is not started until at least 6 payments have been missed.
A borrower who moves home can port the existing rate to a new property if the new mortgage completes within 90 days of repaying the old one.
A borrower can take a payment holiday of up to 6 months in any 12-month period. This version applied during 2020 and 2021 and was withdrawn in January 2022.
A card dispute can be raised up to 120 days after the transaction date. For claims under GBP 500 a provisional credit is applied within 2 working days while the dispute is investigated.
A reimbursement decision on an authorised push payment scam is made within 5 working days. Complex cases can take up to 35 working days. An excess of GBP 100 is deducted from the reimbursement.
A card reported as lost, stolen or compromised is blocked at once and cannot be unblocked. A replacement is ordered in the same call.
Staff who suspect internal fraud use the confidential line on 0800 555 0142 or write to the head of internal audit. Reports can be anonymous.
Full-time staff have 27 days of annual leave, rising to 30 days after 5 years of service. Up to 5 unused days can be carried into the next year and must be used by 31 March.
Staff can self-certify sickness for up to 7 calendar days. A fit note from a doctor is needed from the eighth day. Absence is reported to the line manager before the start of the working day.
Staff studying for a qualification agreed with their manager receive 5 days of paid study leave a year and the exam fee for the first attempt.
The notice period is 3 months for staff at grade D and above and 1 month for all other grades. Notice is given in writing to the line manager.

A normal change to a production system is submitted to the change advisory board at least 5 working days before the planned date. Each change carries a tested rollback plan and a named approver from the business.
An emergency change can be made with the approval of the duty incident manager alone. It is reviewed by the change advisory board within 2 working days after it is made.
No normal changes are made to payment systems between 15 December and 5 January. Emergency changes during the freeze need the approval of the chief technology officer.
During a severity 1 incident the incident manager sends an update every 30 minutes. A post-incident review is published within 10 working days of resolution.
Transaction records are kept for 7 years after the account closes. Recordings of customer calls are kept for 6 years. Marketing consent is refreshed every 24 months.
CCTV footage from branches is kept for 31 days unless it is needed for an investigation. Data about unsuccessful job applicants is deleted after 12 months.
A cashier till holds no more than GBP 4,000. Cash above the limit is moved to the vault, which is opened only under dual control by two members of staff.

A suspected counterfeit note is kept, recorded on form BRN-14C and sent to the cash centre within 2 working days. The customer is given a receipt and is not reimbursed until the note is confirmed genuine.
